title: Stone Pine: Ancient Umbrella Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: The flat-topped pine that gives the Mediterranean its skyline. Istanbul's Ata Fıstık Çamı, about 400 years old, gave a whole hill its name.
intro: The stone pine is the tree that gives the Mediterranean skyline its flat topped silhouette, and it normally does that from a bare trunk ten or fifteen metres up, spreading wider than it grows tall. The one on Florence's Bobolino hillside ignores the rule and stands 31.5 metres. Two on a Setubal street are older than the street and are left over from the woodland it was cut through. Istanbul's Ata Fistik Cami, about 400 years old, gave a whole hill its name and was brought there from the Aegean rather than growing there naturally. On Mallorca the road between Valldemossa and Deià was widened around one rather than through it. Naples has the odd one out: the pine above Mergellina was arguably the most photographed tree on earth for a century, and the tree on that hillside now was planted in 1995 in place of the original.
